name: fn0_refs_rtx-5090
command: python bench/offload_ctx.py run --name fn0_refs_rtx-5090 --gpu 0 --model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf --arms spikes/fn0/arms_refs_rtx-5090.json --rounds 3 --requests fn_full.json --contexts 1024 4096 32768 --server llama-server --resume
method: Batch-1 decode and prefill at fixed contexts, for the expert-offload comparisons (docs/v1-offload.md acceptance 3, D14; docs/v1-flash-next.md D11): every arm loads in a fresh process, runs one untimed warm-up request, then for each context C its requests of a C-token prompt generating 256 tokens, greedy, ignore_eos. Prefill tok/s = C / prompt time; decode tok/s = (tokens - 1) / (last token - first token). Prompts are spans of natural text, the same ids for every engine and round, so an expert cache sees real routing and no prefix cache can reuse one prompt for another: - `--corpus v1` (X): the judge prompt set's token ids, concatenated and cut at fixed, distinct offsets (wrapping),   one request per context; - `--corpus fn` (FN, D11): the text of v1-long, v1-qwen3_5 and v1, concatenated in that order and tokenized with   Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's tokenizer (N tokens); context C (index c in `--contexts`) has the candidate starts   (k * (N // 6) + c * (N // 18)) mod N, k = 0..5, a start inside the warm-up span (the corpus's last 2,048 tokens)   moved past it, and `--spans` picks the candidates timed (default the first 3). The orchestrator writes the warm-up and the timed requests' ids to `requests.json`; workers read only that file.
